==Problem==
Una rolls <math>6</math> standard <math>6</math>-sided dice simultaneously and calculates the product of the <math>6{ }</math> numbers obtained. What is the probability that the product is divisible by <math>4?</math>

<math>\textbf{(A)}\: \frac34\qquad\textbf{(B)} \: \frac{57}{64}\qquad\textbf{(C)} \: \frac{59}{64}\qquad\textbf{(D)} \: \frac{187}{192}\qquad\textbf{(E)} \: \frac{63}{64}</math>

==Solution==
We will use complementary counting to find the probability that the product is not divisible by <imath>4</imath>. Then, we can find the probability that we want by subtracting this from 1. We split this into <imath>2</imath> cases. 

Case 1: The product is not divisible by <imath>2</imath>.

We need every number to be odd, and since the chance we roll an odd number is <imath>\frac12,</imath> our probability is <imath>\left(\frac12\right)^6=\frac1{64}.</imath>

Case 2: The product is divisible by <imath>2</imath>, but not by <imath>4</imath>.

We need <imath>5</imath> numbers to be odd, and one to be divisible by <imath>2</imath>, but not by <imath>4</imath>. There is a <imath>\frac12</imath> chance that an odd number is rolled, a <imath>\frac13</imath> chance that we roll a number satisfying the second condition (only <imath>2</imath> and <imath>6</imath> work), and <imath>6</imath> ways to choose the order in which the even number appears.

Our probability is <imath>\left(\frac12\right)^5\left(\frac13\right)\cdot6=\frac1{16}.</imath>

Therefore, the probability the product is not divisible by <imath>4</imath> is <imath>\frac1{64}+\frac1{16}=\frac{5}{64}</imath>.

Our answer is <imath>1-\frac{5}{64}=\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ \frac{59}{64}}</imath>.

==Solution 2(Pretty much same as above)==

Complementary counting implies that we can have either 0 factors of 2 or just 1 factor of 2.

Case 1: 0 factors of 2

The only odd numbers are 1, 3, 5 on a die so we have these 3 odd numbers with 6 positions so <imath>3^6</imath> ways here.

Case 2: 1 factor of 2

The only even numbers that have only one factor of 2 on a die are 2, 6. On the 6 positions, there are 6 ways to place one of these even numbers and the rest of the 5 positions must be one of the three odd numbers. Since we could have either 2 or 6, we have

<imath>2 \cdot 6 \cdot 3^5 = 4 \cdot 3^6</imath>. 

Thus, we have <imath>3^6 + 4 \cdot 3^6 = 5 \cdot 3^6</imath> cases that don't work.

By complementary counting we get

<imath>1 - \frac{5 \cdot 3^6}{6^6} = 1 - \frac{5}{2^6} = \boxed{\frac{59}{64}}</imath>
